es: Distinguir en un texto de estudio la afirmación (claim), la prueba (evidence) y la opinión, juzgar si una prueba es sólida o solo anecdótica y reconocer las expresiones que señalan cada función.

vocabulary.es: pruebas, datos que apoyan una idea
anecdótico, basado en un caso aislado

teaching.en: A claim is an idea the writer defends, and it stays weak until the writer can back up the claim with evidence.
teaching.es: Una afirmación es una idea que el autor defiende, y sigue siendo débil hasta que el autor puede respaldarla con pruebas.
teaching.explanationEs: Claim es lo que se defiende; evidence es lo que lo apoya. Back up + objeto + with + prueba.
segments: A claim is an idea the writer defends, and it stays
weak until the writer can back up the claim with evidence.
teaching.audioText: A claim is an idea the writer defends, and it stays weak until the writer can back up the claim with evidence.

teaching.en: According to a survey of 300 students, most of them sleep under seven hours, which is the kind of data that supports the claim.
teaching.es: Según una encuesta a 300 estudiantes, la mayoría duerme menos de siete horas, que es el tipo de datos que apoya la afirmación.
teaching.explanationEs: According to + fuente señala una prueba. Una survey y sus data se pueden comprobar.
segments: According to a survey of 300 students, most of them sleep under
seven hours, which is the kind of data that supports the claim.
teaching.audioText: According to a survey of 300 students, most of them sleep under seven hours, which is the kind of data that supports the claim.

teaching.en: Some experts argue that teenagers need more sleep, but what they argue is a claim, not a fact, until it has been tested.
teaching.es: Algunos expertos sostienen que los adolescentes necesitan dormir más, pero lo que sostienen es una afirmación, no un hecho, hasta que se ponga a prueba.
teaching.explanationEs: Argue that introduce la tesis de alguien. Un fact se puede comprobar; una afirmación aún debe probarse.
segments: Some experts argue that teenagers need more sleep, but what they argue
is a claim, not a fact, until it has been tested.
teaching.audioText: Some experts argue that teenagers need more sleep, but what they argue is a claim, not a fact, until it has been tested.

teaching.en: In my opinion, mornings are far too early for teenagers, but an opinion says what someone feels and cannot be checked like a fact.
teaching.es: En mi opinión, las mañanas son demasiado tempranas para los adolescentes, pero una opinión dice lo que alguien siente y no se puede comprobar como un hecho.
teaching.explanationEs: In my opinion y I feel that señalan una opinión: es válida, pero no cuenta como prueba.
segments: In my opinion, mornings are far too early for teenagers, but an
opinion says what someone feels and cannot be checked like a fact.
teaching.audioText: In my opinion, mornings are far too early for teenagers, but an opinion says what someone feels and cannot be checked like a fact.

teaching.en: A single story about one tired student is anecdotal, so it cannot back up a general claim the way a large survey can.
teaching.es: La historia de un solo estudiante cansado es anecdótica, así que no puede respaldar una afirmación general como lo hace una encuesta grande.
teaching.explanationEs: Anecdotal describe un caso aislado: ilustra una idea, pero no la demuestra.
segments: A single story about one tired student is anecdotal, so it cannot
back up a general claim the way a large survey can.
teaching.audioText: A single story about one tired student is anecdotal, so it cannot back up a general claim the way a large survey can.

teaching.en: Writers who assert a sweeping claim, such as «all teenagers are lazy», should name a credible source, because a confident tone is not evidence.
teaching.es: Quienes afirman algo tan general como «todos los adolescentes son vagos» deberían nombrar una fuente creíble, porque un tono seguro no es una prueba.
teaching.explanationEs: Assert suena rotundo; sweeping describe una afirmación demasiado general; credible valora la fuente. La seguridad del tono no sustituye a las pruebas.
segments: Writers who assert a sweeping claim, such as «all teenagers are lazy»,
should name a credible source, because a confident tone is not evidence.
teaching.audioText: Writers who assert a sweeping claim, such as «all teenagers are lazy», should name a credible source, because a confident tone is not evidence.

prompt.es: Lee el texto. ¿Qué función cumple la segunda oración?

choices.text: Evidence: it gives a source and a figure that can be checked.
Claim: it states the main idea that the writer wants to defend.
Opinion: it says how the writer feels about early mornings.

feedback.es: La segunda oración cita una fuente (una encuesta) y una cifra comprobable: es la prueba que respalda la afirmación de la primera.

hint.es: Fíjate en la fuente y en la cifra: son lo que se puede comprobar.

origin.text: Schools should start at nine. According to a survey of 300 students, 68 percent sleep under seven hours on school nights.

prompt.es: Completa: «Según una encuesta a 300 estudiantes, la mayoría duerme poco.»

feedback.es: According to + fuente introduce una prueba y deja claro de dónde sale el dato.

hint.es: Es la palabra que, junto a to, introduce una fuente.

origin.text: Teenagers need more sleep, and, ___ to a survey of 300 students, most of them sleep under seven hours.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En mi opinión, las mañanas son demasiado pronto para los adolescentes.»

answer.text: In my opinion mornings are too early for teenagers

feedback.es: In my opinion abre una valoración personal, que no cuenta como prueba.

hint.es: Empieza por la fórmula que señala una opinión.

prompt.es: Escucha el pódcast y elige qué dato funciona como prueba en el argumento.

choices.text: Her sister's tiredness at eight o'clock in the morning on school days.
The survey of three hundred students who slept under seven hours.
Her view that nine o'clock would be the best start.

feedback.es: La encuesta aporta una fuente y un dato comprobable; la hermana es un caso aislado (anecdótico) y las nueve como hora ideal es una opinión.

origin.audio: In this week's study skills podcast, the host reads out a short argument. Schools, she says, should start later in the morning. To back up that claim, she quotes a survey of three hundred students, most of whom slept under seven hours on school nights. She then adds that, in her own opinion, nine o'clock would be the best time, and that her sister is always exhausted at eight. The host admits that the last detail is only anecdotal, but she thinks the survey is credible.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada oración con la función que cumple en el texto.

pairs: A survey of 500 workers found that 40 percent felt tired.
Workers should be allowed to start later.
I feel that early meetings are a bad idea.
My cousin is always tired at eight.

feedback.es: La encuesta es una prueba; «should» marca la afirmación; «I feel» marca una opinión; el primo es un caso aislado, es decir, una anécdota.

pairs: A survey of 500 workers found that 40 percent felt tired.
Workers should be allowed to start later.
I feel that early meetings are a bad idea.
My cousin is always tired at eight.

prompt.es: Lee el texto. ¿Por qué la tercera oración no sirve como prueba?

choices.text: It repeats the claim in other words without a source.
It gives a fact about the building, but no source.
It reports a personal feeling that nobody can check.

feedback.es: «Personally, I find…» expresa una sensación personal que nadie puede comprobar; la prueba es la segunda oración, con una cifra atribuida al personal.

origin.text: The council should close the library on Sundays. Library staff say that fewer than ten people visit on Sundays. Personally, I find the building cold and dark.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué parte del artículo es la prueba más sólida.

choices.text: The teachers' report linking less homework to lower stress.
The story of her cousin, who now smiles more than before.
Her final comment that homework is a waste of time.

feedback.es: El informe de los profesores aporta datos de muchos alumnos; el primo es un caso aislado y la última frase es una opinión.

origin.audio: A student wrote in the school newspaper that homework should be banned. She claims that pupils who do no homework are happier, and as proof she mentions her cousin, who stopped doing homework last year and now smiles more. Later, she quotes a report from a group of teachers, which found that pupils with less homework reported lower stress. She ends by saying that homework is a waste of time. The editor added a note: the report is credible, but the cousin is only one case.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué da a entender la nota del editor?

choices.text: That the whole article is unreliable and should be ignored.
That only part of the evidence should be taken seriously.
That the student's claim has now been proven correct.

feedback.es: El editor separa lo creíble (el informe) de lo que es solo un caso (el primo): da a entender que una parte de las pruebas pesa más que la otra.

origin.audio: A student wrote in the school newspaper that homework should be banned. She claims that pupils who do no homework are happier, and as proof she mentions her cousin, who stopped doing homework last year and now smiles more. Later, she quotes a report from a group of teachers, which found that pupils with less homework reported lower stress. She ends by saying that homework is a waste of time. The editor added a note: the report is credible, but the cousin is only one case.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hace una afirmación fuerte, pero no puede respaldarla con cifras.»

feedback.es: Back up es el verbo frasal para respaldar una afirmación con pruebas; sin cifras ni fuente, la afirmación queda sin apoyo.

origin.text: The writer makes a bold claim about school uniforms, but she has not given a single figure or source, so she cannot ___ it up.

prompt.es: ¿Qué función cumple «A study of twelve schools found no difference…»?

choices.text: It is a claim that repeats the experts' view.
It is an opinion that supports the experts.
It is evidence that goes against the experts' claim.

feedback.es: El estudio aporta datos comprobables y contradicen la afirmación de los expertos: es una prueba en contra, no una opinión ni una repetición de la tesis.

origin.text: Some experts argue that uniforms improve behaviour in class. A study of twelve schools found no difference in behaviour between schools with and without uniforms. In my view, however, uniforms are a good idea.

prompt.es: Escucha. ¿Por qué solo la tercera reseña ayuda a decidir?

choices.text: Because it offers facts that the reader can check.
Because it is the most positive of the three reviews.
Because it comes from the person who owns the café.

feedback.es: Las dos primeras reseñas son opiniones; la tercera da precios concretos, que son datos comprobables y sirven para decidir.

origin.audio: I have read three reviews of the new café. One calls it the best coffee in town, another says that it is far too expensive, and the third gives the price of every drink on the menu. Only the third can really help me decide.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender «However, the survey did not ask about age»?

choices.text: That cycling to work has no health benefits at all.
That the evidence is weaker than it first looks.
That the survey of 2,000 commuters was badly written.

feedback.es: «However…» introduce una reserva: sin datos sobre la edad o la forma física, los ciclistas podrían ser simplemente más sanos; la prueba pesa menos de lo que parecía.

origin.text: Many people say that cycling to work is healthier than driving. A survey of 2,000 commuters found that cyclists take fewer sick days. However, the survey did not ask about age or health.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una afirmación sin pruebas es solo una opinión.»

answer.text: A claim without evidence is only an opinion

feedback.es: Sin datos ni fuente que la respalden, una afirmación no pasa de ser una opinión.

es: Matizar afirmaciones académicas con verbos, modales y expresiones de cautela (may indicate, it could be argued, to a certain extent, there is limited evidence) sin exagerar lo que permiten los datos.

vocabulary.es: exagerar, afirmar más de lo que permiten los datos
en general, en su mayor parte

teaching.en: The findings may indicate that short naps improve memory, although they are hardly conclusive, since only forty students took part.
teaching.es: Los resultados podrían indicar que las siestas cortas mejoran la memoria, aunque apenas son concluyentes, ya que solo participaron cuarenta estudiantes.
teaching.explanationEs: May indicate apunta a una relación sin afirmarla. Conclusive describe una prueba que cierra la cuestión; aquí no lo es.
segments: The findings may indicate that short naps improve memory, although
they are hardly conclusive, since only forty students took part.
teaching.audioText: The findings may indicate that short naps improve memory, although they are hardly conclusive, since only forty students took part.

teaching.en: It could be argued that homework has a limited effect on learning, particularly when students already study a great deal.
teaching.es: Podría sostenerse que los deberes tienen un efecto limitado en el aprendizaje, sobre todo cuando los estudiantes ya estudian mucho.
teaching.explanationEs: It could be argued that presenta una tesis como discutible. Limited reduce el alcance: el efecto existe, pero es escaso.
segments: It could be argued that homework has a limited effect
on learning, particularly when students already study a great deal.
teaching.audioText: It could be argued that homework has a limited effect on learning, particularly when students already study a great deal.

teaching.en: To a certain extent, online classes help students who work, but the benefit appears to depend on how well they organise their time.
teaching.es: En cierta medida, las clases en línea ayudan a los estudiantes que trabajan, pero el beneficio parece depender de lo bien que organicen su tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: To a certain extent limita el alcance; appear to + verbo base presenta algo como una apariencia, no como un hecho.
segments: To a certain extent, online classes help students who work, but the
benefit appears to depend on how well they organise their time.
teaching.audioText: To a certain extent, online classes help students who work, but the benefit appears to depend on how well they organise their time.

teaching.en: The results suggest that most students prefer quiet places, and by and large this matches what earlier surveys have shown.
teaching.es: Los resultados sugieren que la mayoría de los estudiantes prefiere lugares tranquilos, y en general esto coincide con lo que mostraron encuestas anteriores.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest that apunta en una dirección; by and large generaliza sin excluir excepciones.
segments: The results suggest that most students prefer quiet places, and
by and large this matches what earlier surveys have shown.
teaching.audioText: The results suggest that most students prefer quiet places, and by and large this matches what earlier surveys have shown.

teaching.en: Teenagers tend to sleep later than adults, which is largely due to biology, although habits also play a part.
teaching.es: Los adolescentes suelen dormir más tarde que los adultos, lo cual se debe en gran parte a la biología, aunque los hábitos también influyen.
teaching.explanationEs: Tend to + verbo base expresa una tendencia, no una regla; largely indica que hay otras causas menores.
segments: Teenagers tend to sleep later than adults, which is largely
due to biology, although habits also play a part.
teaching.audioText: Teenagers tend to sleep later than adults, which is largely due to biology, although habits also play a part.

teaching.en: Saying that sleep is the only cause of good grades would overstate the case, because a significant difference in scores is not proof, and memory is merely likely to improve.
teaching.es: Decir que el sueño es la única causa de las buenas notas sería exagerar, porque una diferencia significativa en las notas no es una prueba y la memoria solo es probable que mejore.
teaching.explanationEs: Overstate the case es afirmar más de lo que permiten los datos; likely to + verbo base expresa probabilidad, no certeza.
segments: Saying that sleep is the only cause of good grades would overstate the case, because
a significant difference in scores is not proof, and memory is merely likely to improve.
teaching.audioText: Saying that sleep is the only cause of good grades would overstate the case, because a significant difference in scores is not proof, and memory is merely likely to improve.

prompt.es: Elige la versión cautelosa de esta afirmación exagerada.

choices.text: Short naps clearly improve memory in most of the students we studied.
The findings suggest that short naps may improve memory in some students.
Perhaps short naps might possibly improve the memory of some students.

feedback.es: Combina un verbo (suggest), un modal (may) y una limitación (some); la segunda exagera y la tercera apila matices hasta volverse confusa.

hint.es: Busca una sola idea matizada con un verbo y un modal, sin apilar recursos.

origin.text: Overstated claim: «Short naps improve memory in every student.» The study included only forty students.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los adolescentes suelen dormir más tarde que los adultos.»

feedback.es: Tend to + verbo base expresa una tendencia general, con excepciones posibles.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa «soler» y va seguido de to.

origin.text: Teenagers ___ to sleep later than adults, which is largely due to biology.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En cierta medida, las clases en línea ayudan a quienes trabajan.»

answer.text: To a certain extent online classes help students who work

feedback.es: To a certain extent abre la frase y limita el alcance de la afirmación.

hint.es: Empieza por la expresión que limita el alcance de la afirmación.

prompt.es: Escucha la clase y elige qué ventaja destaca la profesora de la segunda versión.

choices.text: It avoids mentioning the result so that nobody can object to it.
It sounds more confident and therefore easier for readers to believe.
It shows the reader how far the evidence really goes.

feedback.es: La profesora dice que la segunda versión no oculta el resultado, pero indica hasta dónde llega la prueba; no busca parecer más segura ni evitar objeciones.

origin.audio: In a short lecture on sleep, the teacher warns her students against overstating their results. A weak sentence, she says, would be: naps improve memory. A stronger one would be: the findings may indicate that short naps improve memory, at least for students under twenty. She explains that the second version does not hide the result, but it tells the reader how far the evidence goes. Then she adds that, in her experience, students tend to be too sure of their results, not too careful.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada recurso de cautela con su tipo.

pairs: The results suggest that…
Memory might improve with regular sleep.
To a certain extent, the plan works.
There is limited evidence that…

feedback.es: Suggest es un verbo de cautela, might es un modal, to a certain extent es una expresión y there is limited evidence señala que faltan datos.

pairs: The results suggest that…
Memory might improve with regular sleep.
To a certain extent, the plan works.
There is limited evidence that…

prompt.es: Lee los datos. ¿Qué versión del resultado es la más adecuada?

choices.text: There is limited evidence that most students study better in silence.
Most students study better in silence, as the survey has shown.
The survey proves that silence is the best way to study.

feedback.es: Con solo 12 estudiantes y sin más datos, lo adecuado es reconocer que la evidencia es escasa; las otras opciones presentan el resultado como un hecho probado.

origin.text: A survey of 12 students found that nine of them studied better in silence. The sample is tiny, and the survey asked nothing about age or subject.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué corrige la segunda investigadora la frase.

choices.text: The online classes were too short to raise anyone's grades this year.
A small group of interested students cannot prove such a claim.
The first version was too long to fit the draft.

feedback.es: La segunda investigadora señala que la muestra era pequeña y que los alumnos que eligieron las clases en línea ya estaban más motivados: eso no permite hablar de prueba.

origin.audio: Two researchers are discussing their draft. The first says that the results prove that online classes raise grades. The second disagrees: the sample was small, and the students who chose online classes were probably more interested in studying. She suggests a more careful version: the results suggest that online classes may help interested students to a certain extent. The first researcher hesitates, then admits that the second version is more honest, although it sounds less exciting.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué da a entender el primer investigador al decir «more honest»?

choices.text: That his first version had been copied from another study.
That the second version is worse because it sounds boring.
That his first version claimed more than the data allowed.

feedback.es: Llamar «more honest» a la segunda versión admite que la suya afirmaba más de lo que los datos permitían, aunque suene menos emocionante.

origin.audio: Two researchers are discussing their draft. The first says that the results prove that online classes raise grades. The second disagrees: the sample was small, and the students who chose online classes were probably more interested in studying. She suggests a more careful version: the results suggest that online classes may help interested students to a certain extent. The first researcher hesitates, then admits that the second version is more honest, although it sounds less exciting.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sería exagerar decir que las siestas mejoran la memoria de todos.»

feedback.es: Overstate the case es la colocación para afirmar más de lo que permiten los datos.

origin.text: The survey covered only forty students, so it would ___ the case to say that naps improve memory for everyone.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la conclusión mejor matizada para este estudio?

choices.text: The course appears to have raised scores slightly, although without a comparison group the effect is hard to measure.
The course clearly raised scores, so every school should offer it to all of its students from next year.
It could perhaps be argued that the course may possibly have raised some scores for some students.

feedback.es: Combina un verbo de cautela (appears to), un adverbio (slightly) y la limitación del diseño; la segunda exagera y la tercera apila matices sin decir nada claro.

origin.text: An article reports that a four-week course improved scores by six percent in a group of 35 students. There was no comparison group, and the students had chosen the course themselves.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud adoptan los autores ante su propio hallazgo?

choices.text: Confident: they believe the new timetable is the only cause.
Cautious: they accept that other factors may explain the rise.
Dismissive: they think attendance figures are not important.

feedback.es: Reconocen que la asistencia también subió en escuelas sin el nuevo horario y llaman «tentative» a su hallazgo: dejan abierta la posibilidad de otras causas.

origin.text: According to the report, the new timetable appears to have improved attendance, but the authors admit that attendance also rose in schools that kept the old timetable. They therefore describe their finding as tentative.

prompt.es: Escucha. ¿Por qué prefiere la tutora «suggest» a «prove»?

choices.text: Because the word proves is too informal for the kind of essay she marks.
Because her experiment was badly designed in the first place.
Because one experiment can show a pattern but rarely settle a question.

feedback.es: La tutora explica que un experimento, aunque esté bien diseñado, indica un patrón pero rara vez cierra una cuestión: por eso suggest es más exacto.

origin.audio: My tutor underlined the word proves in my essay and wrote beside it: the data suggest, not prove. She said that one experiment, however well designed, can indicate a pattern but can rarely settle a question. I wrote the sentence again, and it sounded less sure, yet it was more accurate.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los resultados apuntan a que la mayoría prefiere sitios tranquilos.»

answer.text: The results suggest that most students prefer quiet places

feedback.es: Suggest that + oración completa presenta los datos como una indicación, no como una prueba.

es: Leer un resumen académico (abstract) e identificar su objetivo, su método y su conclusión cautelosa, apoyándote en las señales de cada parte y detectando las limitaciones que el texto da a entender.

teaching.en: An abstract is a short summary of a study, and it usually follows the order aim, method, results and conclusion, often in fewer than two hundred words.
teaching.es: Un resumen académico es una síntesis breve de un estudio y suele seguir el orden objetivo, método, resultados y conclusión, a menudo en menos de doscientas palabras.
teaching.explanationEs: El abstract condensa todo el estudio: reconocer su orden te permite localizar cada dato.
segments: An abstract is a short summary of a study, and it usually follows the
order aim, method, results and conclusion, often in fewer than two hundred words.
teaching.audioText: An abstract is a short summary of a study, and it usually follows the order aim, method, results and conclusion, often in fewer than two hundred words.

teaching.en: The aim of this study is to examine whether sleep affects exam performance, rather than simply to describe how much students sleep.
teaching.es: El objetivo de este estudio es examinar si el sueño afecta al rendimiento en los exámenes, en lugar de limitarse a describir cuánto duermen los estudiantes.
teaching.explanationEs: The aim of this study is to + verbo base. Examine whether plantea una pregunta; rather than la contrasta con lo que el estudio no hace.
segments: The aim of this study is to examine whether sleep affects
exam performance, rather than simply to describe how much students sleep.
teaching.audioText: The aim of this study is to examine whether sleep affects exam performance, rather than simply to describe how much students sleep.

teaching.en: The sample included 120 participants aged between 16 and 18, who were placed randomly in one of two groups.
teaching.es: La muestra incluyó a 120 participantes de entre 16 y 18 años, que fueron colocados al azar en uno de dos grupos.
teaching.explanationEs: Sample es el grupo estudiado; participants son las personas. Randomly evita que los grupos se formen a propósito.
segments: The sample included 120 participants aged between 16 and 18,
who were placed randomly in one of two groups.
teaching.audioText: The sample included 120 participants aged between 16 and 18, who were placed randomly in one of two groups.

teaching.en: The method was simple: one group followed a strict sleep schedule for two weeks, while the control group kept its usual habits.
teaching.es: El método fue sencillo: un grupo siguió un horario de sueño estricto durante dos semanas, mientras que el grupo de control mantuvo sus hábitos habituales.
teaching.explanationEs: El control group sirve de comparación: sin él no se sabe si el cambio se debe al tratamiento.
segments: The method was simple: one group followed a strict sleep schedule
for two weeks, while the control group kept its usual habits.
teaching.audioText: The method was simple: one group followed a strict sleep schedule for two weeks, while the control group kept its usual habits.

teaching.en: The participants with more sleep achieved a higher score in memory tests, although the difference was small and varied from one individual to another.
teaching.es: Los participantes que durmieron más lograron una puntuación más alta en las pruebas de memoria, aunque la diferencia fue pequeña y varió de un individuo a otro.
teaching.explanationEs: Los resultados se dan con datos (higher score) y a menudo con una reserva (although…).
segments: The participants with more sleep achieved a higher score in memory tests,
although the difference was small and varied from one individual to another.
teaching.audioText: The participants with more sleep achieved a higher score in memory tests, although the difference was small and varied from one individual to another.

teaching.en: The authors conclude that more sleep may improve performance, but they stress that a correlation between sleep and scores does not prove that one causes the other.
teaching.es: Los autores concluyen que dormir más podría mejorar el rendimiento, pero subrayan que una correlación entre sueño y notas no prueba que una cosa cause la otra.
teaching.explanationEs: Conclude that + may: conclusión cautelosa. Correlación no es causa: una relación estadística no prueba una causa.
segments: The authors conclude that more sleep may improve performance, but they stress that a
correlation between sleep and scores does not prove that one causes the other.
teaching.audioText: The authors conclude that more sleep may improve performance, but they stress that a correlation between sleep and scores does not prove that one causes the other.

prompt.es: Lee el resumen. ¿Qué parte es la segunda frase?

choices.text: Aim: it says what question the study wants to answer here.
Conclusion: it says what the authors think the results mean.
Method: it says who took part and how they were grouped.

feedback.es: La segunda frase describe quién participó (sesenta adultos) y cómo se agruparon: es el método; la primera frase expone el objetivo.

hint.es: Fíjate en si la frase dice a quién se estudió y cómo, o qué se quiere saber.

origin.text: This study examines whether a daily twenty-minute walk improves concentration. Sixty adults were placed in a walking group or a control group for four weeks.

prompt.es: Completa: «El objetivo de este estudio es examinar cómo afecta el sueño al rendimiento.»

feedback.es: The aim of this study is to + verbo base es la señal que abre el objetivo de un resumen.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que, con of this study, introduce el objetivo.

answer.text: Many students believe that one long night of study is the best way to prepare for an exam, but research suggests that regular short sessions may be more effective. A survey of 200 college students found that those who studied for forty minutes every day scored ten percent higher than those who studied only before the exam. This appears to show that regular review helps students retain information, although the effect may depend on the subject. For example, languages seem to benefit more from daily practice than essay subjects do. It could be argued that students who study every day are simply more interested in their courses, so the results should be read with care. To a certain extent, a good schedule matters more than the number of hours. In the long run, a short session every day is likely to be a better habit than cramming, but more research is needed.
accepted: Many students believe that one long night of study is the best way to prepare for an exam, but research suggests that regular short sessions may be more effective. A survey of 200 college students found that those who studied for forty minutes every day scored ten percent higher than those who studied only before the exam. This appears to show that regular review helps students retain information, although the effect may depend on the subject. For example, languages seem to benefit more from daily practice than essay subjects do. It could be argued that students who study every day are simply more interested in their courses, so the results should be read with care. To a certain extent, a good schedule matters more than the number of hours. In the long run, a short session every day is likely to be a better habit than cramming, but more research is needed.

Some people think that listening to music while studying improves concentration. However, a study of 120 teenagers suggests that silence may be better for difficult tasks. The teenagers who worked in a quiet room scored eight percent higher on a reading test than those who listened to music. This seems to indicate that music can distract students, although it might help with simple tasks such as copying notes. It could be argued that some students are used to music and feel calmer with it, so the effect may depend on the person. Largely for this reason, the results should be read with care. Nevertheless, there is some evidence that a quiet schedule with short sessions is likely to work better for most students, but the sample was small and more research is needed before we can be sure of it.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. Let me summarise our study. One hundred and fifty students kept a study diary for a month, and the students who reviewed their notes every day scored twelve percent higher in a final test than the others. Some of you may have an objection, so let me reply to one of them: a classmate asked whether these students were simply more interested in their studies to begin with. feedback.es: Una buena respuesta resume el estudio con fidelidad, da una conclusión con recursos de cautela, reconoce la objeción como razonable, admite el límite y mantiene la conclusión.

origin.text: Resume un estudio para tu grupo, da una conclusión cautelosa y responde a una objeción. Estudio: 150 estudiantes llevaron un diario de estudio durante un mes; los que repasaron cada día sacaron un 12 % más en una prueba final. Objeción de una compañera: «Puede que esos estudiantes ya estuvieran más interesados.» Escribe entre 210 y 260 palabras en inglés: un resumen fiel, una conclusión con al menos dos recursos de cautela y una respuesta que reconozca la objeción, admita el límite y mantenga la conclusión.

prompt.es: Escucha el turno de preguntas. ¿Qué actitud muestra la ponente?

choices.text: Defensive: she denies that a control group would have helped her study at all.
Open: she admits the weakness but explains why the result still matters.
Evasive: she changes the subject to avoid the problem.

feedback.es: Admite que los resultados son menos sólidos, explica por qué no hubo grupo de control y recuerda que el patrón se repitió en tres clases: acepta el límite sin abandonar el resultado.

origin.audio: After the presentation, a student asked why the researchers had not used a control group. The speaker replied that a control group would have been the best choice, but that the school had refused to divide the classes. She conceded that the results are therefore less certain, yet she pointed out that the same pattern appeared in all three classes, and that she would welcome anyone who wants to repeat the study.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿por qué no hubo grupo de control?

choices.text: Because the researchers thought it was not necessary.
Because the students refused to take part in the study.
Because the school would not divide its classes.

feedback.es: La ponente explica que el colegio se negó a dividir las clases; no dice que el grupo de control fuera innecesario ni que los alumnos lo rechazaran.

origin.text: The study involved only one school, so it would be a mistake to ___ the results to every student in the country.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta que acepta la crítica sin abandonar la conclusión.

choices.text: That is a fair point and a limitation; nevertheless, the pattern is clear enough to test elsewhere.

feedback.es: Reconoce el límite, mantiene la conclusión con cautela y propone comprobarla en otras escuelas; las otras opciones lo niegan o lo aceptan tan por completo que retiran todo.

origin.text: After the talk, a classmate says: «Your sample came from a single school, so your results cannot be trusted.» The speaker wants to accept the criticism without giving up her conclusion.

prompt.es: Escucha. ¿Qué da a entender la profesora al decir que era la reacción adecuada?

choices.text: That any study from another city is better than one from here.
That one study should be confirmed by others before it is fully trusted.

feedback.es: La profesora aprueba que Tom pida repetir el estudio en otra ciudad: da a entender que un solo estudio no basta para creerlo del todo.

origin.audio: When the teacher asked for objections, nobody spoke for a moment. Then Tom said that the study looked fair, but that he would like to see it repeated in another city before believing it. The teacher smiled and said that this was exactly the right reaction to a single study.
